119.102.3.en: 3- David longs for the face of God, that is, Christ incarnate in the fullness of time, who shines upon him and upon all the believers in the Old and New Testaments, so that all learn His judgments.

119.103.0.en: (Rivers of waters run down mine eyes, because they keep not thy law.

119.103.1.en: Rivers of waters: plural of river, which is a small stream

119.103.2.en: 1- When David was enlightened by the face of God, his feeling was stirred for those far from God, who had not kept His commandments and had plunged into their evils, so he prayed for them and wept over them much. And he expresses the abundance of his weeping by the likeness that many waters ran from his eyes as if they were rivers of waters. By this he moves God's mercies upon himself, and upon those far away, that He may have mercy on them and draw them to Himself.

119.103.3.en: Look to God with many prayers, and then your heart will open to feel the suffering of those far from God, and you will pray for them every day in your prayer; and be confident that your prayer is very precious to Him, so He has compassion on the whole world, for the sake of your prayer, however weak you are.

119.103.4.en: The eighteenth section (Tsadi): Justice and truth (vv. 137-144). The aim:

119.103.5.en: After David experienced the depths of the word of God, the truth and justice in it also drew his heart, especially in the midst of people's wronging one another, so his heart was filled with zeal, and he loved the commandments while feeling his weakness and his need to learn His rights, and he endured afflictions, but remained holding fast to God's commandments.

119.104.0.en: (Righteous art thou, O LORD, and upright are thy judgments. Thy testimonies that thou hast commanded are righteous and very faithful.

119.104.1.en: 1- God is the righteous, holy One, and His word is upright, just and true. It is a light in the midst of the darkness of people's thoughts and their evil works, for the measure to which we return is the word of God, the source of justice, truth and judgment.

119.104.2.en: 2- The wicked describe the word of God as hard and impossible to carry out, and even say that God's judgments are unjust because He permits the wrong that is spread in the world, whereas the word of God carries all the justice and truth in which alone man finds rest. Everyone who believes in God and repents of his sins is enlightened, and discovers that God is the source of justice and uprightness.

119.105.0.en: (My zeal hath consumed me, because mine enemies have forgotten thy words.

119.105.1.en: 1- David loved the word of God and wished that all people would keep it and enjoy it. But he was greatly troubled because the wicked, his enemies, neglected the word of God and walked in evil. So his heart was filled with good zeal for these souls that are being lost and do not enjoy prayer in the house of God, and from the abundance of his ardor the spiritual zeal weighed upon him, until it almost consumed him; that is, he was deeply affected by the wicked turning away from the worship of God in His house.

119.105.2.en: 2- Christ repeated this verse when He was in the Temple and saw the sellers and the people's preoccupation with buying and selling and their neglect of prayer, so He drove out the sellers and rebuked the people (Jn 2:17).

119.106.0.en: (Thy word is very pure: therefore thy servant loveth it.

119.106.1.en: Pure: free of impurities, that is, clean

119.106.2.en: 1- The words of the wicked are vain and false, and they accuse God of injustice, but the truth that David declares is that God's word is pure; it is the only pure word in the world, indeed the source of purity.

119.106.3.en: 2- David loved the pure word of God, which he keeps, and so his heart is purified. And when he writes the purity of the heart he is able to behold God and enjoy fellowship with Him.

119.107.0.en: (I am small and despised: yet do not I forget thy precepts.

119.107.1.en: 1- David was the youngest of his brothers, so in humility he feels that he is small and despised, and therefore he held fast to God's commandments and did not forget them, and by this he became the greatest of the kings of Israel, with a heart like the heart of God. Humility makes a person hold fast to God's commandments.

119.107.2.en: 2- This verse is a prophecy about the Gentiles who would believe in Christ, and feel that they are small and despised and their strength is in holding fast to God's commandments, and so they surpassed the Jews who refused to believe in Christ.

119.108.0.en: (Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.

119.108.1.en: 1- David testifies that God is just and that His word is the source of justice and is the truth itself. And therefore it is the reference of the believers in all their thoughts, speech and conduct.

119.108.2.en: 2- Christ is the Word of God, that is, the Truth, and the source of justice, and He remains for ever shining with His light on those who believe in Him, so that they grow in the knowledge of the truth.

119.109.0.en: (Trouble and anguish have taken hold on me: yet thy commandments are my delights.

119.109.1.en: 1- In holding fast to God's commandments, David met afflictions and lusts because of the wicked around him and the hard circumstances of life. But his holding fast to God's commandments made him experience the delight of fellowship with God, so he forgot his sufferings and was in joy, and his holding fast to the word of God increased.

119.110.0.en: (The righteousness of thy testimonies is everlasting: give me understanding, and I shall live.

119.110.1.en: 1- David concludes this section by declaring that God's testimonies and word are just, and firm for ever, that is, to eternity. They are the permanent source of justice, so he entreats God to give him understanding of them, that he may live with Him. For the life of the righteous is in the knowledge and understanding of the word of God, so they live with uprightness and purity in this world, and then in the age to come.

119.110.2.en: May you review your life in the light of the word of God that you read every day, for it is the source of justice and truth, and by this you discover the uprightness of your works and words, and correct every deviation, so you obtain God's pleasure, and He even grants you His knowledge every day.

119.110.3.en: The nineteenth section (Qoph): Longing for the word of God (vv. 145-152). The aim:

119.110.4.en: Because the word of God is justice and truth, the righteous man longed for it and kept it, and since he was nourished by it his prayers rose to God.

119.111.0.en: (I cried with my whole heart; hear me, O LORD: I will keep thy statutes. I cried unto thee;

119.111.1.en: save me, and I shall keep thy testimonies.

119.111.2.en: David loved prayer, so that it became very deep, as is shown by:

119.111.3.en: 1- It turned into a cry, that is, he held fast to God intensely.

119.111.4.en: 2- With the whole heart, and not only from the lips or the mind, but with all his feelings.

119.111.5.en: 3- Prayer led him to hold fast to worship, that is, the statutes, and to keep them, so he enjoyed individual worship and communal worship.

119.111.6.en: 4- Continuing in prayer and calling upon God.

119.111.7.en: 5- Relying on God and asking salvation from Him alone, that He might rescue him from his afflictions.

119.111.8.en: 6- Asking salvation from God that he might rise above every sin and earthly concern, and he did not ask material requests or passing lusts.

119.111.9.en: 7- Keeping God's testimonies and word and holding fast to them.

119.112.0.en: (I prevented the dawning of the morning, and cried: I hoped in thy word. Mine eyes prevent the night watches, that I might meditate in thy word.

119.112.1.en: Night watches: plural of watch, which is a division of the night. The Jews divide the night into three watches of 4 hours each, while the Romans divide it into four divisions of three hours each.

119.112.2.en: 1- David's longings for God increased, so that he rose from the morning to pray, waiting for God to make him know His word, that he might live by it.

119.112.3.en: 2- David's longings for prayer continued to increase, so that he could not bear to sleep the whole night without praying, and before the night watchman announced the beginning of the watch David would wake, open his eyes and stand to pray, and repeat the word of God and murmur it. This shows the extent of David's attachment to prayer and the word of God by night and by day.

119.113.0.en: (Hear my voice according unto thy lovingkindness: O LORD, quicken me according to thy judgment.

119.113.1.en: 1- In his prayers David asks God to grant him life with Him, but according to God's will, mercy and judgments; David does not ask his own will or any requests, but surrenders his life to God in tranquility, as his heart is free for prayer and the praise of God.

119.114.0.en: (They draw nigh that follow after mischief: they are far from thy law.

119.114.1.en: 1- David describes the wicked who persecute him and pursue him as drawing near to the followers of vice and evil; because the wicked who pursue him love evil and all who do it, and therefore by this conduct they go far from God's law; for what fellowship hath light with darkness? And the Septuagint translation clarifies the meaning of this verse, saying, "They draw nigh in iniquity who pursue me, and they are far from thy law."

119.115.0.en: (Thou art near, O LORD; and all thy commandments are truth.

119.115.1.en: 1- Those who pursue David trouble him, while he is steadfast in God's commandments, and God encourages him by making him feel that He is near to him, so his heart is reassured and comforted, and he is sure that God's commandments are the truth, so his holding fast to them increases, and he is not disturbed by the wicked who pursue him. By this David experienced that the nearer he draws to God, the further he is from evil, whereas those who pursue him on the contrary draw near to evil and go far from God. David is enlightened and knows that God's commandments are truth, whereas those who pursue him have been occupied with evil, and lived in it, and it has become their life.

119.116.0.en: (Concerning thy testimonies, I have known of old that thou hast founded them for ever.

119.116.1.en: 1- David knew and was sure that the word of God was founded by Him of old, that is, from eternity; if God is eternal, His word is also eternal, and therefore firm until today and for ever, so David can rest his life on it, and live by it strong and stable.

119.116.2.en: 2- The eternal word of God is Christ, who has existed from the beginning and who became incarnate in the fullness of time. He is the way, the truth and the life, and faith in Him gives steadfastness, strength and eternal life.

119.116.3.en: Know that God is very near to you; so do not be anxious if afflictions or sins surround you, but cry out to God and He will surely answer you and rescue you; indeed He will comfort your heart in the midst of the affliction as well.

119.116.4.en: The twentieth section (Resh): Life by the word of God (vv. 153-160). The aim:

119.116.5.en: After showing his longings to be with God, and God's drawing near to him to comfort him, David declared his need of God's wisdom and his grief over the wicked for their turning away from His commandments, and asked for life by the word of God, for it is truth and justice.

119.117.0.en: (Consider mine affliction, and deliver me: for I do not forget thy law.

119.117.1.en: 1- David met afflictions and pursuits from enemies so that he came to be in severe humiliation, but his faith in God did not waver, so he asked Him to rescue him. Self-abasement before God, and humility, is the shortest way to the heart of God to obtain His mercies.

119.117.2.en: 2- David saw with the eye of prophecy Christ the Savior, and saw himself as a member of His body, so he resembles Christ the head of the body in His humility, as He endures sufferings to the Cross, and so he came forward in humility toward the Cross to receive the divine mercy.

119.118.0.en: (Plead my cause, and deliver me: quicken me according to thy word.

119.118.1.en: 1- David brings his cause to God the just Judge after human beings had judged evil against him. But he appeals and brings his cause to the supreme divine court, and asks God to free him and release him from the troubling of his enemies, holding to God's promise in His word to exalt and deliver the humble. And here he is, in humility and abasement, asking His mercy according to His promises.

119.119.0.en: (Salvation is far from the wicked: for they seek not thy statutes.

119.119.1.en: 1- Although God desires the salvation of all, and Christ the Savior died for the redemption of all sinners, some sinners refuse repentance and go far from God's commandments, and therefore feel that God is far from them, since they themselves have pushed Him away. And this of course stirs David's grief over them, because they will perish.

119.120.0.en: (Great are thy tender mercies, O LORD: quicken me according to thy judgments.

119.120.1.en: 1- If the sinners have refused repentance and the word of God, and therefore lost His mercies and His salvation, David, on the contrary, drew near to God to enjoy His many mercies and to live by His word. For in proportion as a person draws near to God and asks His mercies, he receives life in God and enjoys His life-giving word.

119.121.0.en: (Many are my persecutors and mine enemies; yet do I not decline from thy testimonies.

119.121.1.en: 1- The sinners were not content to go away from God, but because of their distance from Him they were filled with evil, so they wronged the righteous without cause, persecuted them and troubled them. But the righteous held fast to their deliverer, which is God's testimonies by which they lived, and did not deviate or turn aside from them.

119.122.0.en: (I beheld the transgressors, and was grieved; because they kept not thy word.

119.122.2.en: 1- Since David held fast to the word of God, he was not disturbed by the persecutions of the wicked, and more than this he had compassion on them; because he hated their evil ways, and wished that they would repent and return to the word of God and keep it, and be saved. For the cause of their falling into evil and treachery is their going away from the word of God.

119.123.0.en: (Consider how I love thy precepts: quicken me, O LORD, according to thy lovingkindness.

119.123.1.en: 1- David comes with boldness to God and asks Him to look upon him, to see how David loved His commandments, as it appeared in his words and works. And with the boldness of sonship he asks God to grant him life by His mercy, and not by his deserving. He is humble and does not try to show his righteousness by holding fast to God's commandments, but out of his need he held fast to the commandments, asking the divine mercy and life with God.

119.124.0.en: (Thy word is true from the beginning: and every one of thy righteous judgments endureth for ever.

119.124.1.en: 1- David concludes this section by declaring that the true word of God has existed from the beginning, and is the head and beginning of everything because it is eternal, and to the age, that is, for ever, God's just judgments prevail and lead the world, and the believers enjoy them in the Kingdom. For the Word of God, that is, Christ, is the beginning and the end, and therefore holding fast to Christ the Savior and His life-giving word gives life and joy and the enjoyment of fellowship with God.

119.124.2.en: Read the word of God every day, for it is the measure by which you weigh all your thoughts, words and works, and by which you sort the right from the wrong among the thoughts of the world, so you walk in tranquility, peace and joy.

119.124.3.en: The twenty-first section (Shin): Peace and joy (vv. 161-168). The aim:

119.124.4.en: Life by the word of God drove David to hold fast to it, so it became the gladness of his heart, and he loved it very much, and so he enjoyed inner peace, hoped for God's salvation, and kept His testimonies and acted by them.

119.125.0.en: (Princes have persecuted me without a cause: but my heart standeth in awe of thy word.

119.125.2.en: 1- By the princes David means Saul and his servants, who rose up against him, pursued him and tried to kill him without his having wronged them, or opposed them, or asked to take their place; on the contrary, he was subject to all orders, and helped in killing Goliath and fighting the enemy Philistines. So he is amazed at this persecution, especially since the ruler is expected to care for his people; how then does he turn into an enemy and persecutor?!

119.125.3.en: 2- David did not fear the persecution of the princes; because he feared God and His word, and sought to carry out His law. And whoever fears God has his heart strengthened, so he fears no one whatever his position, since he trusts in God's protection and care, and rises above earthly lusts. And so all God's children in the Old and New Testaments did not fear, whether the prophets and men of God, or the Apostles, martyrs and all the saints.

119.126.0.en: (I rejoice at thy word, as one that findeth great spoil.

119.126.1.en: 1- The fear of God made David hold fast to the word of God, and so he experienced its sweetness, and rejoiced greatly with a joy that he could express only by the comparison that he had obtained great spoil. The fear of God does not prevent a person's joy; on the contrary, it drives out the fear of people, begets joy, and attaches the heart to the divine love. But whoever neglects the fear of God cannot enjoy His love, nor rejoice in His word, as David himself said in the Psalms, "Let my heart rejoice to fear thy name", according to the Septuagint translation (Ps 86:11).

119.127.0.en: (I hate and abhor lying: but thy law do I love.

119.127.1.en: 1- The natural result of the fear of God is that a person loves His commandments, and if a person loves the word of God he hates sin and crookedness, such as lying, and this keeps him from falling into lying. And the farther a person keeps from evil, the more his love for the word of God grows. And likewise, the more he loves the word of God, the farther he keeps from evil.

119.128.0.en: (Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.

119.128.2.en: 1- As a result of the fear of God and the love of His commandments, and many prayers and praises, a person finally receives the greatest grace, which is inner peace, and it is great on condition that the person keep away from stumbling at the word of God, meaning doubt, so he believes the word of God and is therefore able to live by it, and so he enjoys the peace that remains firm within him, whatever disturbances he meets from outside.

119.128.3.en: 2- The love of the law does not only give a person inner peace, but also keeps him from stumbling blocks, that is, sins, since it occupies him with God and lifts him to heavenly things, so he keeps far from evil and does not stumble at it.

119.129.0.en: (LORD, I have hoped for thy salvation, and done thy commandments. My soul hath kept thy testimonies; and I love them exceedingly. I have kept thy precepts and thy testimonies: for all my ways are before thee.

119.129.1.en: 1- Acting by God's commandments made David experience his love for God, so he hopes for His salvation, and a person cannot receive God's salvation and grace unless he strives and keeps His commandments, for grace works with the strivers who hold fast to God, supporting them, moving them and satisfying them.

119.129.2.en: 2- If a person keeps God's commandments he loves them by meditating on them. And if he loves them and his heart is attached to them he is moved to carry them out, and so experiences new depths in them.

119.129.3.en: 3- David hopes for God's salvation which rescues him from his enemies and pursuers, but with the eye of prophecy he also hopes for the salvation of Christ in the fullness of time, and then he advances with longings toward heaven, hoping for complete salvation in eternity.

119.129.4.en: When you read the word of God each day, try to memorize one verse, or meditate on it, for this moves your feelings toward God, and you love His word, and so you become qualified to carry out His commandments, experience the work of His grace in you, and taste the sweetness of His word and of being with Him.

119.129.5.en: The twenty-second section (Tau): Asking for salvation (vv. 169-176). The aim:

119.129.6.en: The peace and joy that David tasted drove him to prayer, relying on God's promise, who wants to draw His children near to Him. So he asked to be before God, praising Him and singing to Him, and asking for His salvation and life with Him, and that He not leave him to go astray because of his sins, because he loves His commandments.

119.130.0.en: (Let my cry come near before thee, O LORD: give me understanding according to thy word. Let my supplication come before thee: deliver me according to thy word.

119.130.1.en: 1- In this last section of the psalm David draws near to God, because he loved Him and loved His commandments very much. But when he drew near he felt his unworthiness of this nearness; yet he loved God, so he entreated Him that his cry might reach Him and come near, and that his requests might also come before Him, as he felt his weakness and his sins, which hinder him from appearing in the presence of God.

119.130.2.en: 2- He asked God to make him understand how to stand before Him, and to grant him the new life in Him, and deliver him from his sins and from everything surrounding him; because he is in great joy at being in the presence of God, and never wants to leave Him.

119.131.0.en: (My lips shall utter praise, when thou hast taught me thy statutes. My tongue shall speak of thy word: for all thy commandments are righteousness.

119.131.1.en: 1- When David found himself near to God and in His presence, his lips overflowed with the praise of God like a spring from which much water flows. And because God taught him His statutes and His worship, in which he experienced fellowship with God, his praises and spiritual songs increased, as he rejoiced in the presence of God.

119.131.2.en: 2- David is in joy because of the justice of God, who granted him to be with Him, and compensated him for the afflictions surrounding him with an enjoyment that cannot be expressed

119.132.0.en: (Let thine hand help me; for I have chosen thy precepts. I have longed for thy salvation, O LORD; and thy law is my delight.

119.132.1.en: 1- David chose God's law to live by it, and this choice is the opposite of the choice of his enemies, who chose evil, and therefore he asks God's help to carry out His commandments and be established in them however much the enemies resist.

119.132.2.en: And when he experienced God's commandments and help he longed to be saved from his sins, the wars of the devil and the resistance of enemies, to be free for the word of God and delight in meditating on it. For this is David's true life, in being with God and enjoying His commandments.

119.132.3.en: 2- The hand of God that David asks for his help is a prophecy about Christ the Redeemer, and he longs for His salvation that He would accomplish on the Cross in the fullness of time, so that He grants him and all the believers the delight of being in Paradise with Him. David's heart was drawn to God, so he crossed time and saw Christ, and even rose to Paradise and the Kingdom.

119.133.0.en: (Let my soul live, and it shall praise thee; and let thy judgments help me.

119.133.1.en: a- David's heart was attached to God and to the praise of His holy name, so he asked Him to grant him the spiritual life, that is, constant existence with Him, that he might continue in His praise by day and by night. He also asked God to help him by His judgments and commandments, so that he would not fall into sin, or concern about this world, or be occupied in any way away from God; because life had become, in David's view, being in constant prayer and praise with Him, indeed he longs for constant praise in the Kingdom of Heaven.

119.134.0.en: (I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek thy servant; for I do not forget thy commandments.

119.134.1.en: Sheep: a beast, but what is meant here is a lamb.

119.134.2.en: 1- After David rose very high and enjoyed, he did not forget his weakness, his unworthiness, his exposure to falling into any sin, and he remembered his previous sins, so he called on God his helper and said to Him, "I have gone astray by my sins like a sheep, and I have no helper but You, O Lord, and I cannot return to You because of my weakness, so seek me Yourself and rescue me, and I have no boldness before You except that I loved Your commandments, and repeat them, and strive to live by them. Despite my weakness and my sins I love You, and I love Your commandments, and I wish to remain in Your presence, praising You all the days of my life and for ever."

119.134.3.en: How beautiful it is to be with God, so do not deprive yourself of meditation and praise every day. Give enough time to prayer, that you may taste the sweetness of fellowship with God, and rise to heaven while you are on earth, and your heart be attached to eternity so that you live for it.

119.134.5.en: 1- They are the psalms from (Ps 120 to Ps 134), which are fifteen psalms

119.134.7.en: a- Four of them are attributed to David, which are (Ps 122, 124, 131, 133).

119.134.8.en: b- One of them is attributed to Solomon, which is (Ps 127).

119.134.9.en: c- The rest of these psalms, ten, have unknown writers.

119.134.11.en: a- When the children of Israel went up to Jerusalem, which is built on five hills, or mountains, and they used to go up to Jerusalem to worship in its Temple, especially at the three great feasts, at which every male of the children of Israel had to appear before the Lord in His Temple, which are the feasts of Passover, Pentecost (the Fifty) and Tabernacles.

119.134.12.en: b- Those returning from the captivity repeated them, declaring their joy at returning to the Temple and its rebuilding.

119.134.13.en: c- The Levites repeat them as they go up the ascending steps from the outer court to the inner court, which number seven, then those going up from the inner court to the house of the Lord, which number eight, and they would stand on each step and say a psalm of the fifteen Psalms of Ascents, and perhaps they remembered the angels ascending on Jacob's ladder in his wonderful dream, and also the fifteen years that God gave to Hezekiah, by which He lengthened his life.

119.134.14.en: d- The priests repeat them as they go up from the Holy Place to the Holy of Holies, that is, from the house to the sanctuary, and the number of these steps is fifteen, so the priests would stand on each step and repeat a psalm of the Psalms of Ascents.

119.134.17.en: a- They include different meanings and have many spiritual purposes suitable for worshipers who pray and love God. A spiritual meaning and purpose can be set for each psalm suitable for the one ascending from earth to heaven, or from the world to the house of the Lord to enjoy being in His presence. And here is one of these meanings:

119.134.18.en: (Ps 120:) "In my distress I cried unto the LORD"... It represents the cry of a person who suffers on earth, but has hope in heaven. (Ps 121:) "I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills"...

119.134.19.en: Meditation on the loftiness of God, His help, and His work in His children.

119.134.20.en: (Ps 122:) "I was glad when they said unto me"...

119.134.21.en: Joy in going up to the house of the Lord, which is a pledge of the heavenly Jerusalem.

119.134.22.en: (Ps 123:) "Unto thee lift I up mine eyes... as the eyes of servants"...

119.134.23.en: The humility of the one ascending and his feeling that he is a servant before his master.

119.134.24.en: (Ps 124:) "If it had not been the LORD who was on our side" Trust in God who supports us in our ascent.

119.134.25.en: (Ps 125:) "They that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion" Reliance on the Lord. (Ps 126:) "When the LORD turned again the captivity of Zion, we became like those who are comforted" Divine comforts in the midst of the sufferings of the ascent:

119.134.26.en: (Ps 127:) "Except the LORD build the house" The Lord builds our new house, that is, our new nature in Baptism:

119.134.27.en: (Ps 128:) "Blessed is every one that feareth the LORD" The Lord's blessings for those who trust in Him:

119.134.28.en: (Ps 129:) "Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth" The sufferings of the ascent, in which one experiences the victory of the Lord, for the one who bears the Cross experiences the Resurrection: (Ps 130:) "Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O LORD" The cry of the sinner with hope in God:

119.134.29.en: (Ps 131:) "LORD, my heart is not haughty" Humility is the way of ascent:

119.134.30.en: (Ps 132:) "LORD, remember David, and all his afflictions."

119.134.31.en: The Lord dwells in the heart, and so a person finds his rest:

119.134.32.en: (Ps 133:) "Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!"

119.134.33.en: Fellowship among the believers encourages those who ascend:

119.134.34.en: (Ps 134:) "Behold, bless ye the LORD" The praise of those ascending, as they are filled with the Holy Spirit and have reached God:

119.134.35.en: b- The fifteen psalms can be divided into five units in their meanings, each unit containing three psalms, and these units are:

119.134.36.en: (Ps 120-122:) The need for the Lord the Savior.

119.134.37.en: (Ps 123-125:) Faith and reliance on the merciful Lord.

119.134.38.en: (Ps 129-131:) Endurance, repentance and humility are the marks of those who ascend.

119.134.39.en: Songs of Ascents (Ps 132-134:) The praise of God who dwells among His children.

119.134.40.en: 5- The prayers of the Agpeya: All the Psalms of Ascents are found in the prayers of the Agpeya; they are prayed in the Agpeya in the Vespers and Compline prayers, in addition to their repetition in the Veil prayer and the Midnight prayer. Why do you pray them at these times?

119.134.41.en: a- The Vespers prayer: It includes the first ten Psalms of Ascents, which are (Ps 120-129), and they tell us of the hope in God of those of the eleventh hour, to whom we ascend in humility, faith and reliance, that He may gladden our hearts and comfort us in the midst of the sufferings of life.

119.134.42.en: b- The Compline prayer: It includes the remaining five Psalms of Ascents, which are (Ps 130-134), and they tell us of the repentance of the sinner before his day ends and he meets God, so he comes forward in humility asking God to dwell in his heart and in the midst of His Church, to lift hearts to praise.

119.134.43.en: c- The Veil prayer: It includes (the two psalms (Ps 121, Ps 129) of the Vespers prayer, and the five Psalms of Ascents found in the Compline prayer. So when the veil of night comes upon us the one who prays lifts his heart to God, after enduring the sufferings of the day, and comes forward in repentance and longing to be with God in the quiet of the night.

119.134.44.en: d- The Midnight prayer: It includes all the Psalms of Ascents, for at midnight a person rises in prayer above earthly things, and turns to heavenly things in humility, repentance and longing for God.

119.134.46.en: a- All the Psalms of Ascents are short, to suit the one who prays as he ascends from one step to another, so he can concentrate on them and grasp their meanings.

119.134.47.en: b- The words of these psalms touch a person's feelings, because he is ascending and his heart is attached to the house of God and to being with Him.

119.134.48.en: c- There are relations between the meanings of these psalms that can be understood from the fourth item of this introduction.

119.134.49.en: The Helper in afflictions - a song of ascents. Introduction:

119.134.50.en: 1- Its writer: The title of this psalm does not mention the name of the writer, so it is one of the orphan psalms whose writer is unknown.

119.134.51.en: 2- This psalm shows that the writer suffers from the deceit and hypocrisy of those around him and much false speech, so that he felt his exile in their midst. He represents the cry of a righteous man who wants to live with God in a world full of evil.

119.134.52.en: 3- You sense in this psalm tranquility and faith in the heart of its writer and a wonderful peace, and this confirms his strong relationship with God.

119.134.53.en: 4- This psalm suits every person who passes through affliction or is exposed to problems from those around him.

119.134.54.en: 5- This psalm is considered one of the Messianic psalms; because it expresses the psychological sufferings to which Christ was exposed from the Jews who persecuted Him, deceived Him and tried to catch Him in a word, hiding behind false words of praise (v. 2).

119.134.55.en: 6- This psalm is found in the prayers of the Agpeya in the Vespers and Midnight prayers, for it expresses the sufferings that the spiritual person endured throughout the day, and he casts them before God in reliance on Him, to regain his peace.
